title: Dashboard tiles load quickly and one slow tile does not hold up the others
custom_preconds:
1. Sign in on the build under test as an Admin user. Admin holds every permission, including Reports, so Reports and Dashboard both show in the top menu.
  2. In the top bar choose the busiest location you can reach (the one with the most invoices and clocked time), so every tile has real work to do.
  3. Have a stopwatch or a phone timer ready.
custom_steps:
1. Click Work Orders in the top menu so you start away from the Dashboard.
  2. Start the stopwatch and click Dashboard in the top menu.
  3. Stop the stopwatch when all six tiles (Revenue, Billing Efficiency, Technician Efficiency, Technician Utilization, Sales by Customer, At Risk Customers) show a figure.
  4. Write down the time.
  5. On each of the four top tiles and on Sales by Customer, click the range pill and choose Last 12 Months.
  6. Watch the tiles while each one reloads and note whether any tile stays blank or waits for another tile.
  7. Repeat steps 1 to 4 two more times and write down each time.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Each time, all six tiles show their figures in about one second. A load that clearly takes several seconds, again and again, is reported.
  • The tiles fill in on their own: no tile waits for another tile before it shows its figure.
  • This part cannot be checked by hand: the measured targets (95 of every 100 first loads within 1 second, each tile's server time within 250 ms, no single query over 500 ms, and a 2-second cut-off that fails only the slow tile). Write "targets not checked by hand" in the result comment and pass or fail on what you can see.
  • Making one tile slow or fail on purpose is not possible by hand. Write "slow-tile cut-off not checked by hand" in the result comment.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-490; Dashboard v1 Technical Implementation Plan (sources/Dashboard-v1-Technical-Implementation-Plan.md, 2026-09-16), NFR-001, read in full 7 Oct 2026. The tech plan informs and never overrules the PRD; Dashboard v1 PRD Confluence 788430850 v42 (read 7 Oct 2026) states no speed target.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • Tech plan NFR-001: “No dashboard query may exceed 500 ms; anything above is treated as a defect and alerted. Per-tile server time targets p95 ≤ 250 ms; the six-tile first load targets p95 ≤ 1 s (a slight overrun is acceptable). Every dashboard statement carries a 2 s `MAX_EXECUTION_TIME` circuit breaker, and a query that trips it fails only its own tile (FR-021)”

Last checked against build v26.39.1-09be696 on 10/2/2026.

AUTOMATION: HOLD - not manually testable (performance budget and per-tile circuit breaker are developer/automated checks)
